candidates.label: Ipilimumab-induced dermatomyositis (immune-related adverse event)
missing_or_uncertain: Biopsy negative for inflammation, but performed after corticosteroid treatment; skin biopsy not mentioned

candidates.label: Paraneoplastic dermatomyositis associated with malignant melanoma
missing_or_uncertain: Temporal relationship with ipilimumab suggests drug-induced rather than paraneoplastic

candidates.label: Drug-induced lupus with myositis (from ipilimumab)
missing_or_uncertain: Rash is more dermatomyositis-like; no other lupus features; Jo-1 negative but not specific

candidates.label: Immune checkpoint inhibitor-associated myositis (without skin involvement)
missing_or_uncertain: Skin rash present, so myositis alone is incomplete

candidates.label: Corticosteroid-induced myopathy (type II fiber atrophy)
missing_or_uncertain: Elevated CK and MRI hyperintensity are not typical of steroid myopathy; rash unexplained

response.rationale: The temporal association with ipilimumab (skin symptoms within 2 weeks, second course 14 months later) strongly supports an immune-related adverse event. The photodistributed rash, elevated CK, MRI muscle hyperintensity, and proximal weakness are classic for dermatomyositis. The negative biopsy is explained by prior corticosteroid treatment, which can suppress inflammation. Paraneoplastic dermatomyositis is less likely given the clear drug trigger. Other candidates are less consistent with the full clinical picture.
